description: In jsrsasign's DSA verification (src/dsa-2.0.js:238-248), the FIPS 186-4 requirement 0 < s < q is implemented with a non-strict upper bound, so s = q is accepted. jsbn's `modInverse` returns 0 rather than throwing when the input is non-invertible, so w = s^-1 mod q becomes 0, forcing u1 = u2 = 0 and v = (g^0 * y^0) mod p mod q = 1. The attacker-chosen constant signature (r=1, s=q) therefore satisfies v == r for every message hash and every public key. This is a universal forgery: any DSA-signed data verified with jsrsasign can be spoofed without the private key. A PoC confirms the forged signature verifies on arbitrary messages under jsrsasign 11.1.1.
reproduction: 1. Obtain the target's public DSA parameter q (part of the public key / domain params).
2. Construct the DER-encoded signature with r = 1 and s = q.
3. Submit this signature alongside any message/payload of the attacker's choosing.
4. jsrsasign computes w = q^-1 mod q = 0 (jsbn returns 0), so u1 = u2 = 0, v = 1 = r, and verification succeeds.
technical_details:
Hi Kenji --

I've found a vulnerability that's looks quite similar to the recent

CVE-2026-4599/4600/4601 fixes in 11.1.1---the same file

(unfortunately) has one more. The verify-side range check at

src/dsa-2.0.js line 244 allows s=q, and jsbn's modInverse returns 0

for non-invertible inputs rather than throwing, so (r=1, s=q) is a

universal forgery: it verifies against any message under any DSA

public key.

(Up-front disclosure: an LLM found this bug. I validated it myself

against jsrsasign 11.1.1 from npm and confirmed the forged signature

verifies on arbitrary messages. I stand by this report personally.)

The bug is the same off-by-one shape as CVE-2026-4601, which fixed the

r=0/s=0 case on the *sign* side. That is, the verify side has:

    // src/dsa-2.0.js:238-248

    // 3.1. 0 < r < q

    if (BigInteger.ZERO.compareTo(r) > 0 || r.compareTo(q) > 0)    //

allows r=0, r=q

        throw "invalid DSA signature";

    // 3.2. 0 < s < q

    if (BigInteger.ZERO.compareTo(s) >= 0 || s.compareTo(q) > 0)   //

allows s=q  <-- BUG

        throw "invalid DSA signature";

    // 4. get w where w = s^-1 mod q

    var w = s.modInverse(q);    // jsbn returns 0 when s == 0 (mod q)

But FIPS 186-4 section 4.7 requires strict inequalities---the comment above

exactly says this!---but s.compareTo(q) > 0 rejects only s > q, not s = q.

When s = q, modInverse is being asked for the inverse of q mod q, which

doesn't exist. The jsbn library handles this by returning 0

(ext/jsbn2.js:517, the x.signum() == 0 branch after x = this.mod(m)).

The verify code never checks w != 0. Therefore we can calculate that:

    w  = 0

    u1 = z*0 mod q = 0

    u2 = r*0 mod q = 0

    v  = (g^0 * y^0) mod p mod q = 1

Setting r = 1 makes v == r hold for every message hash z and every

public key y. The forged signature is the constant DER sequence

SEQUENCE { INTEGER 1, INTEGER q }.

Running the attached poc.js (sorry---base64 encoded to evade gmails

malware filter) against jsrsasign 11.1.1 should give hte following:

    [*] Testing jsrsasign 11.1.1

    [*] Forged signature (r=1, s=q): 301a020101021500996f967f6c8e388d...

      verify(hash=0000000000000000...) = true

      verify(hash=deadbeefdeadbeef...) = true

      verify(hash=aaf4c61ddcc5e8a2...) = true

      verify(hash=3c52e0e5c87f4b6a...) = true

    >>> VULNERABLE: (r=1, s=q) verifies on all messages <<<

The r check at line 240 has the same two off-by-ones (it allows r=0

and r=q), but neither of these leads to a bug.  I've included both in

the patch for completeness since they're the same FIPS 186-4

requirement.

The fix is a short change on line 244 (and the same on 240):

    -   if (BigInteger.ZERO.compareTo(s) >= 0 || s.compareTo(q) > 0)

    +   if (BigInteger.ZERO.compareTo(s) >= 0 || s.compareTo(q) >= 0)

A patch is attached.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Nicholas
title: [security] off-by-one DSA signature validation error; different than CVE-2026-45{99,01,02}
